html: Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against artery walls. When it stays high, the heart works harder and the risk of heart attack, stroke and kidney disease goes up.

image.alt: Illustration of a heart with a pulse line
image.caption: High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so regular checks matter.
image.title: Illustration of a heart with a pulse line

html: A reading has two numbers, such as 120/80. Your care team will explain what your readings mean and what target is right for you.

• Limit salt (sodium) and processed foods
  • Stay active most days of the week
  • Limit alcohol and avoid tobacco
  • Take medicines as prescribed
Call 911 for a very high reading with chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness or weakness, vision changes, or difficulty speaking.
